cards.text: Now Bildad the Shuhite, one of Job's three friends (Job 2:11), replies to Job. He opens with "How long until you end these speeches?" And then, friend... he gives a WHOLE SPEECH.

cards.question: Bildad tells Job to do something first, and then they can talk. What is it?
I think Bildad feels insulted here. He asks Job why the friends are regarded as cattle, as ___ in Job's sight.

cards.text: Bildad calls Job someone who tears himself in anger. Then he asks Job a question big enough to hold the whole landscape.

cards.question: Bildad asks if the earth should be forsaken on Job's account, or the rocks moved from their place. What is Bildad's point?

answers.text: The world won't bend for Job
Job should go plant new fields
Job should build a stone altar

cards.question: Now Bildad paints a picture of the wicked man, and he starts with the wicked man's lamp. What happens to it?

cards.text: Bildad says, "His vigorous stride is shortened, and his own schemes trip him up." That's tripping over your own shoelace, except the shoelace is your PLAN.

cards.question: In Bildad's picture, enemies drag the wicked man into a net.

cards.text: Then the traps pile up: one seizes his heel, a snare grips him, a noose hides in the ground, and a trap lies in his path. That's crossing a dark living room barefoot, and EVERY step is a problem.

cards.question: In Bildad's picture, the wicked man finally finds a safe place where nothing frightens him.

cards.text: His strength runs out, and calamity stands ready at his side. Bildad says it devours patches of his skin, and the firstborn of death devours his limbs.

cards.question: Bildad says the wicked man is torn from the shelter of his tent. Who is he marched off to?

cards.text: Bildad says fire resides in the wicked man's tent and burning sulfur rains down on his dwelling. I LOVE a hot oven, friend, but THAT is not an oven.

cards.question: Then Bildad's picture changes: the ___ beneath the wicked man dry up, and the ___ above him wither away.
Bildad says the memory of the wicked man perishes from the earth.

cards.text: Bildad says the wicked man is driven from light into darkness and chased from the inhabited world. First he's torn from his tent, and now he's out of the whole world.

cards.question: Bildad says the wicked man leaves plenty of children behind to carry on his name.

cards.text: Bildad says those in the west are appalled at the wicked man's fate, while those in the east tremble in horror. That's the WHOLE map shaking, friend, both sides at once.

cards.question: Bildad wraps up his speech. Whose dwelling does he say all of this describes?

answers.text: One who does not know God
One who has lost his flocks

cards.text: That's Bildad's whole speech, and Job heard every word of it. Hold on to your apron, friend, because this conversation is FAR from over.
